SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW.rationale: Common positive divisors of a,b are unchanged by a=bq+r and by absolute values. Positive remainders strictly decrease, final divisor divides both initial inputs. Excluding (0,0), one zero input has gcd equal to absolute value of the other. Divisors36 and Euclidean trace252,105->42->21->0 recomputed. 8 and15 coprime though composite. Recursive identity bu+rv=d with r=a-qb gives av+b(u-qv)=d; abs(r)<abs(b) even for Python negative divisor, base returns(abs(a),sign(a),0). Every pair of signed inputs retains positive gcd. Every composite <=n has a prime divisor<=sqrt(n); crossing multiples from p*p is complete since smaller multiples were already removed. Trial division retains product of extracted factors times remaining integer; after p*p>remaining, remaining>1 must be prime. Empty product1 and n<2 sieve handled.
